set_aside.unit: A18: Accepted decision A18 — Budget and snapshot invariants
set_aside.subject: INV-028 activation refusal
set_aside.text: “activating a budget version without an allocated section is refused and writes nothing”
set_aside.question: Does activation fail whenever any existing allocation targets a section absent from the candidate version, or only when the candidate version has no allocated section at all?
options: Refuse if even one allocation targets a section without a plan in the candidate version.
Refuse only if none of the candidate version's sections has an allocation.
Apply some other meaning to “without an allocated section.”
set_aside.default_guess: Refuse if any allocation targets a section absent from the candidate version.

witness.initial: Project P has an expense allocated to section S1; candidate budget version V contains a plan for S2 but no plan for S1.
events: A staff operator asks to activate V.
outcomes: Activation is refused because the allocation to S1 would be unresolved.
Activation succeeds because V does contain a section and the phrase is read as requiring only some allocated section.
witness.observer: The staff operator and subsequent readers of P's active budget.

set_aside.unit: A28: Accepted decision A28 — Clock policy (accepted Factory spec, 2026-08-09; one clock source, coordinator 2026-11-07)
set_aside.subject: CLK-001 supplied timestamp representation
set_aside.text: The normative rule says supplied times are kept as “the same instant, stored offset-naive UTC,” while the Required test says each supplied time is “stored as supplied.”
set_aside.question: Must a supplied offset-aware datetime be normalized to offset-naive UTC before storage, or must its supplied representation be preserved?
options: Normalize it to the equivalent offset-naive UTC datetime.
Preserve the supplied offset-aware representation.
Accept only already-naive UTC inputs so the two instructions coincide.
set_aside.default_guess: Normalize to the equivalent offset-naive UTC datetime and interpret “as supplied” as preserving the instant.

witness.initial: A snapshot publication supplies published_at as 2026-11-08T12:00:00+02:00.
events: The authenticated producer publishes the snapshot.
The portal accepts and stores it.
outcomes: The portal stores 2026-11-08T10:00:00 as an offset-naive UTC datetime.
The portal stores 2026-11-08T12:00:00+02:00 unchanged, or rejects it because unchanged storage would violate the offset-naive rule.
witness.observer: A repository reader and the CLK-001 verification check.

set_aside.unit: A28: Accepted decision A28 — Clock policy (accepted Factory spec, 2026-08-09; one clock source, coordinator 2026-11-07)
set_aside.subject: wall-clock reads by operations with no time use
set_aside.text: CLK-002 says “an operation takes one wall reading,” while the surrounding rules qualify the reading as being “for its own timestamps” and the Required tests cover “time-dependent operation[s].”
set_aside.question: Must an operation that writes no timestamp and performs no current-time comparison still read the wall clock exactly once?
options: Every operation, including pure reads and health checks, takes one wall reading.
Only an operation that writes a portal-owned timestamp or performs a current-time comparison takes one wall reading.
set_aside.default_guess: Only time-dependent operations take a wall reading.

witness.initial: The database contains a project whose overview can be built without any expiry check or timestamp write; a counting clock source starts at zero reads.
outcomes: The operation reads the wall clock once although it does not use the value.
The operation performs no wall-clock read because it has no time-dependent work.
witness.observer: The counting clock source and a contract test for build_project_overview.

set_aside.unit: A28: Accepted decision A28 — Clock policy (accepted Factory spec, 2026-08-09; one clock source, coordinator 2026-11-07)
set_aside.subject: elapsed-clock rate-limit state
set_aside.text: The elapsed reading “measures the viewer-entry rate-limit window” but “is never stored”; the Required test narrows this only to “no record written by the request holds it.”
set_aside.question: May the rate limiter retain elapsed readings or values derived from them in process memory across requests, and if so which forms of retention are allowed?
options: The prohibition concerns persisted records only; in-memory elapsed readings may be retained.
The raw reading may not be retained, but derived limiter state such as a window deadline or token-bucket state may be retained.
Neither the reading nor a value derived from it may be retained across requests.
set_aside.default_guess: Allow non-persistent limiter state, including elapsed readings or derived deadlines, while forbidding persistence in portal records.

witness.initial: No viewer-entry requests have occurred and the elapsed clock reads 100.0 seconds.
events: A viewer makes one entry request.
The same viewer makes another entry request at elapsed time 101.0 within the configured window.
outcomes: The limiter retains cross-request in-memory timing state and applies the configured rate limit to the second request.
The implementation treats “never stored” literally, retains no timing state, and cannot classify the second request from the two readings as belonging to one window.
witness.observer: The viewer making the second entry request.

set_aside.unit: A28: Accepted decision A28 — Clock policy (accepted Factory spec, 2026-08-09; one clock source, coordinator 2026-11-07)
set_aside.subject: CLK-002 host-clock source check
set_aside.text: The source check names `datetime.now`, `datetime.utcnow`, `datetime.today`, `date.today`, `time.time`, `time.monotonic` “and their variants.”
set_aside.question: Which APIs, aliases and indirect calls count as variants, and what source-check rule demonstrates that the clock source is the only reader of either host clock?
options: Check only calls to the six named APIs.
Also reject aliases and equivalent standard-library APIs such as `time.perf_counter` and `os.clock_gettime`.
Enforce an import or dependency boundary that prevents every module except the clock source from reaching any clock backend.
set_aside.default_guess: Enforce a dependency boundary and reject aliases or equivalent wall/elapsed clock APIs outside the clock-source module.

witness.initial: A module outside the clock source contains no call to any of the six literally named APIs.
events: An implementer reads elapsed time using `time.perf_counter()`.
outcomes: The check treats `perf_counter` as a monotonic-clock variant and fails.
The check examines only the named calls and passes.

set_aside.unit: A32: Accepted decision A32 — Dependency pins and their vulnerability check (owner 2026-11-06: current service behaviour accepted; technical decisions delegated)
set_aside.subject: DEP-002 withdrawn advisories
set_aside.text: The normative rule excludes an OSV entry that “is not withdrawn,” but the Required test says “a listed version” does not start, without preserving the withdrawn-entry exception.
set_aside.question: Does an installed version listed only by a withdrawn OSV entry pass or block the deploy?
options: Pass, because withdrawn entries do not meet the normative definition of a known vulnerability.
Block, because the Required test says any listed version prevents start.
set_aside.default_guess: Pass when every matching OSV entry is withdrawn.

witness.initial: The built image contains distribution D version 1.0; OSV returns one entry listing D 1.0 as affected, and that entry has a withdrawal timestamp.
events: The deploy reads that OSV response.
The release gate evaluates the image.
outcomes: The image passes because the sole entry is withdrawn.
The image is refused because its installed version is listed as affected.
witness.observer: The deployment operator waiting for the service to start.

set_aside.unit: A32: Accepted decision A32 — Dependency pins and their vulnerability check (owner 2026-11-06: current service behaviour accepted; technical decisions delegated)
set_aside.subject: DEP-002 unmatchable advisory data
set_aside.text: The Required test says “unreadable or unmatchable advisory data” does not start the service, but neither “unmatchable” nor its distinction from a valid no-vulnerability result is defined.
set_aside.question: Exactly which OSV responses or package-resolution cases are unmatchable and therefore fail closed?
options: Only malformed or unsupported OSV data that prevents determining whether the installed version is affected.
A valid empty OSV result for an installed PyPI distribution is also unmatchable.
Any discrepancy between the installed distribution name/version and OSV's package identifiers is unmatchable.
set_aside.default_guess: Treat only data that cannot be parsed or cannot yield a definite affected/not-affected verdict as unmatchable; a valid empty result passes.

witness.initial: The image contains PyPI distribution D version 1.0, and its OSV query succeeds with a valid empty vulnerability list.
events: The deploy gate evaluates the response.
outcomes: The gate records a determinate no-known-vulnerability result and starts the service.
The gate calls the absence of a matching advisory “unmatchable” and refuses to start.

set_aside.unit: A32: Accepted decision A32 — Dependency pins and their vulnerability check (owner 2026-11-06: current service behaviour accepted; technical decisions delegated)
set_aside.subject: vulnerability-check tool handoff
set_aside.text: “The tool that runs the check is a deployment procedure, not a portal rule, carried to the deploy route.”
set_aside.question: Which receiving state owns the still-open tool/procedure choice, what decided execution must it implement, and which check confirms that handoff?
options: Name and configure a specific OSV-aware release-gate tool in a designated deployment state.
Specify a tool-independent deployment contract in a designated receiving state and let the route choose any implementation satisfying it.
Keep the choice informally delegated to the deploy route without a named receiving state.
set_aside.default_guess: Carry a tool-independent release-gate contract to a specifically named deployment state, with DEP-002's witness as its conformance check.
